note.explanation: ATP is a nucleotide made of adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups. The bonds between its phosphate groups are high-energy bonds. When the outer phosphate bond breaks, ATP becomes ADP, inorganic phosphate (Pi) separates, and about 7.3 kcal of energy per mole is released. Cells use energy from food to join ADP and Pi and make ATP again. For example, ATP can break down to release energy for a cell process, while energy from food can be used to rebuild ATP.
examples: ATP + H₂O → ADP + Pi + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)
ADP + H₂O → AMP + Pi + energy (7.3 kcal/mole)
note.simple: ATP is like a small energy packet. Breaking off its outer phosphate releases energy, and cells can use energy from food to attach a phosphate again.

written.text: What do ATP and ADP mean? What are the roles of these molecules for the cellular metabolism?
written.finalAnswer: ATP means adenosine triphosphate and ADP means adenosine diphosphate. ATP stores and transfers usable energy; when ATP breaks down to ADP and Pi, energy is released for cell processes. Cells use energy from food to combine ADP and Pi to make ATP.

explain.title: What ATP is
explain.body: Your textbook defines it this way: “Cells use a special energy currency for their reactions. This currency is a nucleotide called adenosine triphosphate (ATP).” ATP has three subunits: adenine, ribose and three phosphate groups.

explain.title: How ATP releases energy
explain.body: The covalent bonds between two phosphates are high-energy bonds. When the outer phosphate bond breaks, inorganic phosphate (Pi) separates, ATP becomes ADP, and energy is released. Breaking one phosphate bond releases about 7.3 kcal per mole of ATP.

explain.title: How ATP is made again
explain.body: Cells get energy from the oxidation of food. They use this energy to combine ADP with Pi and form ATP. Your textbook summarizes: “ATP is made during energy-releasing processes and is broken down during energy-consuming processes.”

explain.title: Why ATP is called an energy currency
explain.body: ATP transfers energy between metabolic reactions. A cell can make ATP when energy is available, then break it down when a process needs energy.

mistakes: Do not say that ATP is made of adenine and phosphate only; include ribose and all three phosphate groups.
Do not say the whole ATP molecule breaks apart when energy is released; the outer phosphate bond breaks, forming ADP and Pi.
Do not confuse ATP with ADP: ATP has three phosphate groups, while ADP has two.
Do not omit the energy value or give the wrong unit: the section states about 7.3 kcal per mole of ATP.
